strategy: Add one closed concrete-host-bootstrap@1 declaration, a built-in trusted factory that verifies the declaration and Starter registration before assembling existing adapters/checkpointer/Orchestrator, and an atomic host-init authoring command that installs and registers a verified Starter then emits the bootstrap. GitHub remains optional and credential values remain environment-only. Missing WriteAuthorityGuard remains fail-closed.

changes.responsibility: validate and load a bounded bootstrap, create SQLiteSaver, assemble existing Providers, and return StarterHostOrchestrator
changes.reason: one trusted concrete factory is currently missing

changes.responsibility: atomically install/register a verified Starter and generate a sealed project-relative bootstrap
changes.reason: operators should not hand-write assembly files

changes.responsibility: expose host-init with explicit project and optional GitHub settings
changes.reason: initialization needs one canonical authoring command

changes.responsibility: allow local-only Provider assembly while preserving optional GitHub integration
changes.reason: read-only/local operation must not require an unused token

changes.responsibility: publish the closed generated declaration contract
changes.reason: bootstrap must be reviewable and versioned

changes.responsibility: prove initialization, exact validation, assembly, environment credential loading, and fail-closed boundaries
changes.reason: the security-sensitive composition boundary needs focused and negative tests

changes.responsibility: document lifecycle, generated files, commands, extension points, and standalone boundary
changes.reason: operators need a concrete project workflow

changes.responsibility: link the built-in factory and initializer
changes.reason: transport documentation must show the completed bootstrap path

unchanged_boundaries: Starter verification and registration remain package identity authorities
Capability activation remains Provider selection authority
WriteAuthorityGuard remains the only mutation authorization boundary and is not created by initialization
LangGraph remains Workflow runtime and TaskRun remains completion authority
no merge adapter or automatic merge is added
customer application source and runtime dependencies remain independent
forbidden_repairs: Do not accept executable module paths or credential values in Host commands.
Do not embed tokens in generated files or output.
Do not create an allow-all or duplicate WriteAuthorityGuard.
Do not treat initialization, activation, Graph END, CI green, or Quality green as TaskRun completion.
Do not overwrite an existing installation or partially leave a failed initialization.
Do not change product source, completion policy, or merge authority.
required_invariants: all bootstrap paths are bounded beneath the project workspace
Starter registration is reverified on every factory load
SQLite checkpointer is durable and project-local
GitHub integration is optional and token values come only from the named environment variable
missing GitHub credentials block configured integration instead of silently downgrading
missing write authority blocks mutating Skill and Provider dispatch
initializer refuses overwrite and cleans partial output

focused: local-only initialization emits verified generated artifacts
built-in factory assembles the real Orchestrator and durable checkpointer
configured GitHub integration loads only a named environment token
counterexamples: unexpected fields, unsafe paths, stale fingerprints, missing registration, missing token, and overwrite attempts fail closed
unconfigured write authority is never fabricated
regression: authoring, Starter runtime, Provider bootstrap, Host Orchestrator, Host transport, schema, and required skill-only profiles remain green

risks: LocalProcess profile execution remains explicitly allow-listed and target_ref-selected by existing adapter policy.
The one-shot process owns the SQLite connection for the duration of one command; durable state is on disk.
Mutating workflows require a separately configured existing WriteAuthorityGuard and are intentionally blocked by the built-in default factory.
rollback_plan: Remove the bootstrap/initializer modules, schema, tests, and documentation link, and restore GitHub-required Provider bootstrap signature. Existing manual trusted factories and all lower runtime components continue to work.
